item.title: Talanov dynamics and chirp-controlled rogue-wave formation for the vector nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.08786v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the focusing vector nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation, or Manakov system, for a pair of coupled initial conditions with compactly supported, concave parabolic density profiles and phases depending quadratically on the spatial coordinate. We focus on the natural class of self-similar solutions generated by such profiles, whose dispersionless evolution we refer to as Talanov dynamics. We extend the criterion for blow-up in finite time, first established for a single field, to the Manakov case. For arbitrary initial chirps in the two fields, we provide closed-form expressions for their evolution, and an explicit expression for the time of the gradient catastrophe, if it occurs, and we classify the effect of the coupling on the catastrophe. Depending on the initial chirps, the two fields may catastrophise, or relax, as each would if decoupled. However, coupling can also force the catastrophe in fields that would otherwise relax if decoupled. For identical initial supports, and in the presence of dispersion, we numerically show that the same dispersionless criterion determines, in the semiclassical regime, whether the fully dispersive solution relaxes or develops a rogue wave in each field, whose onset time is accurately predicted by the corresponding dispersionless catastrophe time, in direct analogy with the scalar case. As chirp and amplitude are relatively easy to control experimentally, we expect these results to be relevant to experiments in nonlinear optics and Bose-Einstein condensates, extending to coupled systems observations made for the scalar equation.
item.dc:creator: G. Ortenzi, G. Roberti, M. Sommacal

item.title: Discrete four-component massive Thirring model
item.description: arXiv:2611.07686v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct a discrete four-component massive Thirring model (MTM) within the Cauchy matrix framework. A connection between the dependent variables of the discrete four-component MTM and those of the discrete Mikhailov model is established. Taking two successive continuum limits, we first reduce this discrete four-component MTM to its semi-discrete counterpart, and further arrive at the continuous four-component MTM. Solving the determining equation set enables us to construct AKNS-type and KP-type solutions, including explicit soliton solutions and multiple-pole solutions. Imposing the local reduction and nonlocal reduction on the discrete four-component MTM yields the discrete MTM and the reverse-(n,m) discrete MTM, respectively. For these two reduced systems, we prove that the former admits AKNS-type solutions, whereas the latter possesses both AKNS-type and KP-type solutions.
item.dc:creator: Xiao-gang Mu, Jing Wang, Song-lin Zhao

item.title: On deforming and breaking integrability
item.description: arXiv:2603.17018v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper we study nearest-neighbour deformations of integrable models. After expanding in the deformation parameter, we identify four possible types of deformations. First there are deformations that simply break or preserve integrability. Then we find two different subtle cases. The first case is where the deformation is only integrable if all orders of the deformation parameter are taken into account. An example of these are the long-range deformations that appear in holographic models. The second case is when the deformation is perturbatively integrable to some order in the deformation parameter but can not be extended to an integrable model. In this paper we work this out for the XXZ spin chain and discuss the level statistics of each of these cases. We find numerical evidence that the onset of chaos occurs differently in each of these models. For the perturbatively integrable models, we find that the deformation strength at which chaos appears demonstrates a volume-scaling intermediate between strong and weak integrability breaking models.
item.dc:creator: Ysla F. Adans, Marius de Leeuw, Tristan McLoughlin

item.title: Mersenne Representation, the Conolly Sequence, and Soliton Profiles over Finite Fields
item.description: arXiv:2607.22202v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the canonical skew-binary representation of nonnegative integers, whose positional weights are the Mersenne numbers \(2^{k}-1\), and its decomposition into the binary and nonbinary sides. The nonbinary values, arranged in increasing order, form the OEIS sequence A055938, and their successor structure gives a direct proof of the relation with the OEIS sequence A080578 that is recorded as conjectural in the OEIS entry for A080578. The resulting formulas show that the Conolly sequence describes both sides of the decomposition: a shifted Conolly sequence is the counting function of the binary side, while the same sequence gives the increasing enumeration of the nonbinary side. We then develop the parent map, truncation blocks, truncation remainders, and the Mersenne tau function associated with this representation. The parent map is conjugate to deletion of the lowest digit. Differences of the Mersenne tau rows recover the parent iterates and the counting function, and they give formulas for digit reconstruction and for a diagonal tau defect. Finally, we revisit a known finite-depth one-soliton family of the finite-field BBS. The Mersenne combinatorics is used directly to reconstruct a global integer-valued traveling-wave profile and to prove an integer window-counting theorem. Reduction modulo \(3\) yields the corresponding finite-field traveling-wave solutions. We also construct an integer-valued traveling-wave tau function whose front values are given by the Mersenne tau rows. The resulting construction shows how the combinatorics of a number representation can enter directly into the reconstruction of solutions of an integrable system.
item.dc:creator: Fumitaka Yura
